incidente.resumo: On February 2 (year not stated), an OWASA plant operator accidentally commanded the fluoride feed pump to 80 percent instead of the normal 8-12 percent; a correction twelve seconds later did not register, and the pump appears to have overfed fluoride for about 3.25 hours. A level of 5.90 mg/L was recorded, 1.9 mg/L above drinking water standards. With a water main break the next day, this led to a water shortage. The text does not say how the overfeed was stopped or supply restored.
servicos_afetados: OWASA drinking water supply (Orange County: Chapel Hill and Carrboro)

descricao.texto: A lead operator at the plant noticed the extra high levels but did not take corrective action.
trechos: A lead operator at the plant noticed the extra high levels "but did not take corrective action, leading to the issue not being resolved until after 2:40 p.m."

gatilho.texto: At 11:43 a.m. on February 2, a plant operator accidentally instructed the fluoride feed pump to increase its feed rate to 80 percent, compared with a normal operating range of about 8-12 percent.
trechos: at 11:43 a.m. on February 2, a plant operator accidentally instructed the plant's fluoride feed pump to increase its feed rate to 80 percent, compared with its normal operating range of about 8–12 percent.

descricao.texto: The operator tried to change the command about twelve seconds later, but the change did not register; according to the report, the pump appears to have operated significantly above the subsequent commanded speed for approximately 3.25 hours.
trechos: The operator tried to change the command about twelve seconds later, but according to the report, the change didn't register.
The pump appears to have operated at a rate significantly greater than the subsequent commanded speed for approximately 3.25 hours, resulting in a fluoride overfeed condition,

fatores_contribuintes.texto: A major water main break the next day (February 3), together with the extra fluoride dosage, prompted the water shortage; customers could not use or drink their water for more than twenty-four hours.
trechos: The extra fluoride dosage, plus a major water main break the next day, prompted a water shortage in Orange County that closed businesses, placed Chapel Hill and Carrboro under states of emergency, and sent residents scrambling to buy bottled water.
Customers were unable to use or drink their water for more than twenty-four hours.

acoes.texto: Already done: OWASA says it has stopped adding fluoride to the water; the agency is reviewing its policies and seeking public input before reintroducing it.
trechos: OWASA says it has stopped adding fluoride to the water
the agency is reviewing its policies and seeking public input before reintroducing it to the water supply.

acoes.texto: The OWASA board agreed that OWASA would develop solutions to prevent the particular failures, assess outage risks more broadly, improve water system resiliency, and review communication practices during critical events.
trechos: the Board agreed that OWASA would develop solutions to prevent the particular failures of last week, assess outage risks more broadly and take action to improve the water system resiliency, and review communication practices of OWASA and its partners during critical events.
